meta.title: May and the Broken Badge
meta.textType: story: the theme of a story

paragraphs: On Monday, the Explorers made badges for the school market. Each badge had a paw print on a gold flag. Teacher Kim gave Lily a pen and a list. "Write the name and the surname of each buyer," she said. The children wanted to sell all twenty badges.

On Thursday, Teacher Kim asked May to fetch the box of badges from the office. May carried the box in her arms. It was a big box, and it was not light. In the hall, her foot hit a chair, and the box fell. Nineteen badges were fine, but one was broken. May looked around, and nobody saw her. She put the broken badge in her bag.

In the library, Teacher Kim counted the badges. The library was quiet. "There are nineteen," she said. "Are you sure, May? I thought that there were twenty." May did not say anything. She felt hot, and she was very worried. Lily looked at her, but she did not ask.

During the market, May sold three badges, but she did not smile. The broken badge was heavy in her bag. It was a long afternoon. At the end of the day, she decided to tell the truth. "Teacher Kim, I have just remembered something," said May. "I dropped the box, and I broke one badge." "I am sorry. It is in my bag."

Teacher Kim smiled at her. "Thank you for telling me, May," she said. "A badge can break, and that is not a big problem." "The truth is more important than a gold badge." Lily gave May a small smile, and Mia took her hand. Leo took the broken badge and said, "I can fix it with glue." May felt better, and now she smiled. The next Thursday, they sold the twentieth badge. Mia wrote the buyer's name on the list.
text.summary: The Explorers make gold badges to sell at the school market. May breaks one badge and hides it, but she decides to tell Teacher Kim the truth, and the theme is that telling the truth is the right thing to do.
